headline: Approved September 3 minutes; discussed Labyrinth weed control and a possible DEEP trail grant request.
summary: The financial report showed a combined balance of $32,130.53. Members discussed a trail cleanup work party, a DEEP recreational trail grant, and weed control on the Labyrinth. The only motion recorded was to approve the September 3, 2026 minutes, and it passed.
decisions: Approved the minutes of September 3, 2026 by motion, which passed.

Item 4: Co-Chair Announcements  
We have a booth at Celebrate Wallingford festival, October 3-4. Booth #67. Cathy will give the pass 
to Tom so he can drive in and unload materials. 
 
Our next trail cleanup work party is scheduled for Sunday, October 18 (rain date Sunday, October 
25). Cathy is not available that day, so someone needs to contact Jose at Dunkin and pick up coƯee 
(regular and decaf) and doughnuts. We need wood chips for the ﬁrst side trail; David will ask tree 
services: Wallingford Tree/K&J/Paradise Tree/Mt. Carmel (and get Public Works permission and 
police notice to allow truck on trail). Cathy will contact schools to get student volunteers. David will 
contact Mr. D at Lyman Hall VoAg for tractor drivers. 
 
Mary is looking for someone with experience using a come-along lever to move trees that are 
blocking the river. 
 
The CT Trail Symposium takes place Friday, October 2, at SCSU.

Item 8: Other Business  
Fred invited landscaper Ted Greiner to talk about invasive control and weed control on the 
Labyrinth. He recommends “Spruce” brand weedkiller made of saltwater and detergent. The new 
Roundup formula does not have glyphosate, but a combined triclopyr/diquat dicot-and-monocot-
killer. A roofer’s torch can burn weeds, but it leaves carbon. “Crew” granular herbicide keeps seeds 
from germinating. A non-woven landscape fabric can be laid down under stone dust, with Crew 
applied once or twice a year. Inexpensive labor can be found on social media site Nextdoor.com. 
“SiteOne” is a nearby landscaper supplier. “Dimension” is an herbicide to control crabgrass.
